newsitem.title: UK: Colombia dock strike deal hits rally on coffee.
newsitem.headline: Colombia dock strike deal hits rally on coffee.

text.p: World coffee prices retreated on Thursday after a powerful rally when they soared 20 percent in just three days, easing from the highs on profit taking and news that a Colombian dock worker's strike had ended.
London March futures for Robusta type coffee ended at $1,542 a tonne, 28 cents down on Thursday's close of $1,570.00. However, coffee remains sharply up from where it ended 1996 at $1,235.

Workers at key grower Colombia's Buenaventura port, which handles around 60 percent of Colombias's coffee exports, and where a backlog of over 305,000 60-kg bags have accumulated, were due to resume work on Friday.
The backlog would take at least five days to clear, Buenaventura port authorities said.

But news of a vote to strike by 800,000 Colombian workers in sectors from telecommunications to public administration, coupled with an ultimatum from truck drivers who service the port that they will strike if a promised hike in freight rates is not forthcoming, fuelled fears of a further export backlog.
Profit taking followed confirmation of news of a new export curb of 1.3 million 60-kg bags for the period January-June by producer nations in a bid to underpin prices.

Elsewhere in commodity markets gold steadied after a new slide on Thursday to a 40-month low to fix stronger during the London afternoon above a $350.00 support level at $352.20, $4.20 up on Thursday's fix.
The yellow metal traded at 1620 GMT at $353.35 an ounce, while Platinum also edged up on Thursday's 40-month low to fix $1 stronger at $357.75 an ounce.

In industrial metals markets copper settled around intra-day lows at $2242.50 per tonne after London Metal Exchange stocks rose by 12,775 tonnes, over double market expectations, and closed the London afternoon session at $2,241.50.
London March futures for the world benchmark Brent Blend of crude oil traded within a range with no major news.
Chicago wheat futures hovered around Thursday's 376-cent level.
